context.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system processes card-not-present authorizations to detect fraud in real-time and provides case management for suspicious transactions. It is designed for mid-size payment processors to balance risk mitigation, sub-50ms latency, and compliance.

## Key Elements
- **Payment Gateway / Core Processing System:** External system sending real-time authorization requests.
- **Fraud Analyst & Merchant Support:** Internal users reviewing flagged cases and handling disputes.
- **Data Scientist / Fraud Modeler & Risk Manager:** Internal users updating rules, models, and auditing decisions.
- **API Gateway & AWS Lambda:** Compute containers executing stateless scoring logic.
- **Amazon DynamoDB & ElastiCache (Redis):** Data containers for low-latency feature stores and transaction state.
- **Amazon SQS & Amazon EventBridge:** Containers for asynchronous event routing and case management.
- **Amazon S3 Object Lock:** Tamper-evident storage container for 7-year audit trails.

## Relationships
- **Payment Gateway to API Gateway:** Sends real-time authorization requests via gRPC/REST over TLS.
- **API Gateway to AWS Lambda:** Invokes scoring functions synchronously.
- **AWS Lambda to DynamoDB & Redis:** Queries features and stores evaluation results via TCP.
- **AWS Lambda to Amazon SQS:** Publishes review cases asynchronously.
- **Users to Web Portals:** Accesses case management, rule updates, and audit logs via HTTPS/TLS.

## Technology Stack
- **AWS Lambda / AWS Fargate:** Stateless compute ensuring rapid scaling within budget.
- **Amazon DynamoDB / ElastiCache (Redis):** Sub-10ms data stores for low-latency feature access.
- **Amazon SQS / EventBridge:** Managed messaging for reliable asynchronous case routing.
- **Amazon S3 Object Lock (Compliance Mode):** Immutable storage guaranteeing tamper-evident 7-year audit logs.
- **AWS X-Ray & Amazon CloudWatch:** Observability tools for distributed tracing and latency tracking.

## Rationale
Fully managed serverless AWS services minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team while easily handling 3,000 TPS under a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Strict isolation of management planes and use of low-latency data stores ensure P99 latency remains below 50ms while satisfying PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year audit requirements.

## Overview
[The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud before approval and provides case management for analyst reviews. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS, and a 7-year tamper-evident audit trail within a €25,000 monthly AWS budget.]

## Key Elements
- [Fraud Analyst & Risk Manager (Users)]
- [Payment Gateway / Core Processing System (External System)]
- [API Gateway / Ingestion Service Container]
- [Real-Time Scoring Engine Container]
- [Case Management Backend Container]
- [Fraud Analyst SPA (React on Amazon S3 / CloudFront)]
- [Model/Rule Deployment Pipeline Container]
- [Compliance Export Container (AWS Lambda)]
- [Primary Operational Datastore (Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2)]
- [Audit & Feature Store (Amazon S3 with Object Lock)]

## Relationships
- [Payment Gateway to API Gateway / Ingestion Service via gRPC/REST over TLS]
- [API Gateway to Real-Time Scoring Engine via gRPC over TLS]
- [Fraud Analyst SPA to Case Management Backend via HTTPS/REST]
- [Case Management Backend to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL via SQL over TLS]
- [Real-Time Scoring Engine to Amazon S3 Audit Store via AWS SDK / HTTPS]
- [Compliance Export Container to Amazon S3 Audit Store via Amazon Athena]

- [Go: Used for API Gateway to ensure minimal GC pauses and high concurrency for 3,000 TPS.]
- [Rust / Java with GraalVM: Powers Real-Time Scoring Engine for ultra-low latency sub-50ms P99 responses.]
- [Amazon ECS Fargate: Runs container workloads with auto-scaling based on CloudWatch gRPC queue metrics.]
- [Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (Serverless v2): Manages transactional data within the €25k/month budget.]
- [Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Provides WORM-compliant, tamper-evident 7-year audit logging.]
- [ArgoCD (GitOps): Automates deployments for the 3-engineer team without manual intervention.]

## Rationale
[This architecture combines high-performance languages (Go, Rust/GraalVM) and serverless AWS infrastructure to meet strict sub-50ms latency and 3,000 TPS demands cost-effectively. Utilizing S3 Object Lock and Aurora Serverless ensures PCI-DSS compliance and a 7-year tamper-evident audit trail while keeping operational overhead minimal for a three-person engineering team.]

API Gateway / Ingestion Service Containe.analysis:
## Overview
The API Gateway / Ingestion Service Container is a Go-based edge service running on Amazon ECS Fargate that ingests, tokenizes, and routes payment authorization requests while enforcing strict latency and security constraints. It securely processes 3,000 requests per second with sub-50ms P99 latency while maintaining PCI-DSS compliance and tenant isolation.

## Key Elements
- Edge Router & TLS Terminator (Go)
- Tokenization & Payload Scrubber (Go)
- Local Rate Limiter & Throttle (Go)
- Ingestion API Handler & Circuit Breaker (Go)
- Usage Metering Emitter (Go)
- AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT) Sidecar

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Core Processing System -> Edge Router & TLS Terminator: Sends payment authorizations [gRPC/REST over TLS 1.3]
- Edge Router & TLS Terminator -> Tokenization & Payload Scrubber: Forwards raw incoming payloads [In-memory Go channels]
- Tokenization & Payload Scrubber -> Local Rate Limiter & Throttle: Passes scrubbed payloads [In-memory Go channels]
- Local Rate Limiter & Throttle -> Ingestion API Handler & Circuit Breaker: Forwards validated requests [In-memory Go channels]
- Ingestion API Handler & Circuit Breaker -> Real-Time Scoring Engine Container: Dispatches requests for fraud scoring [gRPC over TLS with Circuit Breaker]
- Usage Metering Emitter -> AWS Kinesis Data Firehose: Asynchronously streams usage metadata for billing and SLA tracking [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Go (Golang): Selected for high concurrency, low memory footprint, and minimal GC pauses to meet sub-50ms P99 latency.
- Amazon ECS Fargate: Chosen for serverless container orchestration within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget, operated by a three-engineer team.
- Go `sync.Map`: Implements local per-merchant rate limiting, eliminating external cache infrastructure (Redis) to reduce cost and operational complexity.
- AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT): Provides scraper-less metrics and trace export to Amazon CloudWatch.
- AWS Kinesis Data Firehose: Decouples usage metering metrics from the critical request path.

## Rationale
This architecture uses Go on ECS Fargate to achieve high-throughput, low-latency transaction processing within strict budget and team constraints. Local rate limiting, tokenization at the edge, and asynchronous metering ensure PCI-DSS compliance and tenant isolation without adding operational overhead.

Real-Time Scoring Engine Container.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud to protect merchant revenue while enforcing PCI-DSS compliance and 7-year auditability. The Real-Time Scoring Engine Container delivers sub-50ms P99 fraud scoring decisions at 3,000 TPS within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

## Key Elements
* Request Router & Token Masker (Rust): Validates schemas and strips PCI data.
* Feature Aggregator (Rust): Fetches real-time velocity metrics via Amazon ElastiCache Serverless.
* Inference Executioner (Rust with ONNX Runtime): Evaluates pre-compiled ML models and deterministic business rules.
* Circuit Breaker & Fallback Handler (Rust): Enforces 40ms timeouts and fails-open to "review".
* Audit & Feature Store (Amazon S3 with Object Lock): Stores 100% immutable audit logs and features for 7 years.

## Relationships
* API Gateway / Ingestion Service Container -> Request Router & Token Masker: Forwards authorization requests [gRPC over TLS]
* Feature Aggregator -> Amazon ElastiCache Serverless: Fetches real-time velocity metrics [RESP over TCP]
* Inference Executioner -> Audit & Feature Store: Writes audit logs, model versions, and feature explanations [AWS SDK / HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
* Rust: Chosen for memory safety and zero-cost abstractions to guarantee sub-50ms P99 latency.
* ONNX Runtime: Enables high-performance, in-process machine learning model inference.
* Amazon ElastiCache Serverless: Provides high-availability Redis caching within budget constraints.
* Amazon ECS Fargate: Runs serverless container workloads without manual infrastructure management.

## Rationale
Decomposing the scoring engine into optimized Rust components with local caching achieves the required 3,000 TPS at sub-50ms latency. Strict decoupling of audit logging from performance tracing ensures 100% compliance with 7-year retention rules within fixed cost limits.

Case Management Backend Container.analysis:
## Overview
[The Case Management Backend Container provides case review workflows and audit logging for fraud analysts reviewing suspicious payment authorizations. It is built to satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability while maintaining a low-cost, serverless footprint on AWS.]

## Key Elements
* Case API Router / Controller (Node.js/TypeScript)
* Workflow & Assignment Engine
* Audit & Activity Logger
* Metrics Publisher

## Relationships
* Fraud Analyst SPA -> Case API Router: Sends API requests for case reviews [HTTPS/REST]
* Workflow Engine -> Primary Operational Datastore: Writes transactional state [SQL over TLS]
* Metrics Publisher -> Amazon CloudWatch: Publishes EMF telemetry [Asynchronous in-process emission]

## Technology Stack
* Node.js/TypeScript: Selected for rapid case-management feature development by a 3-engineer team
* AWS ECS Fargate: Chosen for serverless container orchestration within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget
* Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2: Utilized for transactional case states and secure SQL over TLS storage
* Amazon CloudWatch EMF: Adopted for zero-infrastructure operational metrics and dashboard generation

## Rationale
[Decomposing the container into in-process modules avoids the operational overhead of managing secondary caching or messaging clusters like Redis. This design strictly adheres to the 25,000 EUR budget, requires minimal maintenance from three engineers, and ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 security.]

## Overview
The Compliance Export Container provides scheduled, automated generation of standardized CSV and JSON audit trails to satisfy 7-year regulatory retention and PCI-DSS compliance. It operates within a cost-effective, serverless architecture managed by a three-engineer team.

## Key Elements
* Compliance Export Container (AWS Lambda)
* Athena Query Orchestrator (Python / boto3)
* Schema Formatter Component (Python / Pandas)
* Presigned URL Notifier
* Amazon Athena
* Audit & Feature Store (Amazon S3 with Object Lock)
* Amazon S3 Compliance Bucket
* Amazon SNS & Amazon SQS DLQ
* Amazon EventBridge

## Relationships
* Compliance Export Container -> Amazon Athena: Executes scheduled audit queries [HTTPS / AWS SDK]
* Compliance Export Container -> Audit & Feature Store: Queries tamper-evident compliance logs [Amazon Athena]
* Compliance Export Container -> Amazon S3 Compliance Bucket: Writes formatted CSV/JSON audit reports [HTTPS / AWS SDK]
* Compliance Export Container -> Amazon SNS: Publishes export status and secure download links [AWS SDK]
* Amazon EventBridge -> Compliance Export Container: Triggers scheduled compliance exports [Cron / AWS Events]
* Compliance Export Container -> Amazon SQS DLQ: Captures unhandled execution failures for analysis [AWS SDK]

* AWS Lambda: Serverless execution environment chosen to maintain the fixed €25k/month infrastructure budget.
* Amazon Athena: Serverless query service used to process heavy 7-year compliance datasets without always-on compute.
* Python with boto3 and Pandas: Lightweight runtime and data manipulation libraries selected for streaming and formatting query results within memory limits.
* Amazon S3 Object Lock: Tamper-evident storage ensuring immutable audit logs for regulatory compliance.

## Rationale
Serverless execution via AWS Lambda and Amazon Athena eliminates idle infrastructure costs, fitting the strict €25k/month budget for a three-engineer team. Scoping exports to standardized CSV/JSON packages via automated streaming prevents memory bottlenecks while fulfilling strict PCI-DSS and 7-year auditability mandates.

## Overview
The Primary Operational Datastore manages transactional data, case workflows, and decision logs for the Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system. It ensures high-performance fraud scoring and secure case management within a strict fixed infrastructure budget.

## Key Elements
- Case Management Schema & Repository Component
- Transaction & Decision Log Component
- Encryption & Masking Proxy Component
- Amazon RDS Proxy
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2

## Relationships
- Case Management Backend Container -> Case Management Schema Component: Reads/writes analyst workflows and overrides via [SQL over TLS]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine Container -> Transaction & Decision Log Component: Writes decision payloads and scores via [SQL over TLS / Connection Pooling]
- Transaction & Decision Log Component -> Audit & Feature Store (S3): Streams aged partitions older than 30 days via [AWS SDK / S3 API]
- Amazon ECS Fargate Containers -> Amazon RDS Proxy: Routes and pools database connections via [TCP]

## Technology Stack
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2: Selected for auto-scaling capabilities to fit the 25,000 EUR/month budget.
- Native PostgreSQL pgcrypto and Row-Level Security (RLS): Implements column-level encryption and data tokenization to meet PCI-DSS compliance without extra infrastructure.
- Amazon RDS Proxy: Manages connection pooling to handle high transaction spikes without database crashes.

## Rationale
Decomposing the datastore internally enables strict PCI-DSS isolation and cost-effective 7-year audit retention via automated S3 offloading. This architecture maintains sub-second performance for 3,000 TPS while respecting the constraints of a three-engineer team.

Audit & Feature Store.analysis:
## Overview
The system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time while providing case management for analysts and 7-year immutable audit logs. It is operated by a three-engineer team on AWS under a strict €25,000 monthly budget.

## Key Elements
- Audit Log Store (Amazon S3 with Object Lock, S3 Lifecycle to Glacier)
- Feature Store (Amazon DynamoDB with native TTL)
- Audit Query Engine (Amazon Athena with AWS Glue Data Catalog)
- Asynchronous Ingestion (Amazon Kinesis Firehose)
- Infrastructure & Deployment (Terraform, ArgoCD)

## Relationships
- Real-Time Scoring Engine Container -> Feature Store: Low-latency point lookups [AWS SDK / HTTPS over TCP]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine Container -> Amazon Kinesis Firehose: Asynchronous batch delivery of audit payloads [HTTPS]
- Amazon Kinesis Firehose -> Audit Log Store: Batched persistence of tamper-evident logs [S3 API / HTTPS]
- Compliance Export Container / Risk Managers -> Audit Query Engine: Serverless SQL audits [Amazon Athena]

## Technology Stack
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Ensures WORM-compliant, tamper-evident 7-year audit retention (R-06).
- Amazon DynamoDB: Provides single-digit millisecond feature reads (R-04) and automated TTL pruning for cost control.
- Amazon Kinesis Firehose: Decouples audit writing from the critical path to protect P99 latency.
- Amazon Athena: Enables serverless SQL querying over S3 logs with zero operational overhead.
- Terraform & ArgoCD: Automates infrastructure provisioning and GitOps deployments for a three-engineer team.

## Rationale
This architecture decouples low-latency scoring operations from heavy compliance storage to satisfy sub-50ms performance requirements. Utilizing serverless and managed AWS services keeps operational overhead minimal for a three-engineer team while strictly enforcing PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year audit constraints within budget.
